packages/rekordbox-live/src/os2l.ts.content: Using `lastIndexOf(":")` breaks bare IPv6 hosts: `'::1'` is parsed as host `':'` and port `1`, so the server binds the wrong interface/port. In addition the parsed port is never range-checked against `OS2L_PORT_MIN`/`OS2L_PORT_MAX`, so out-of-range values (or `NaN` from a non-numeric suffix such as `'host:abc'`) are passed straight to `server.listen`. Parse `[host]:port` / bare host explicitly and validate the port falls within the advertised range.

Two error handlers are registered on the same server: this permanent listener plus the `server.once("error", reject)` below. On a listen failure both fire, so `setStatus({state:"failed"})` is called twice (and a third time from the catch in `onStart`), and because the permanent listener is never removed in `onStop` a late socket error after shutdown will overwrite the provider status again. Keep a single handler and detach it in `onStop`.

`sendFeedback` writes to every tracked socket without checking `writable`/`destroyed`. A socket that was reset or half-closed by the peer will emit `ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED`/`EPIPE`, which is only swallowed by the socket's `error` listener; guard the write (skip !socket.writable or cleaned-up sockets) so feedback is not silently lost.

`decodeOs2lText` re-implements the exact parsing `ingestChunk` performs lower in this file (splitting, `JSON.parse`, the same zod schema, and identical `bad OS2L ...` message formatting) but through a different code path (`safeParse` vs `try/catch`). Any schema or message-format change now has to be made in two places and the two can drift. Extract a single parse helper and have both entry points call it.

The `slot === 1 || ... || slot === 4` guard is always true for the finite numbers JSON normally carries, and the `null` return is only reachable for a non-finite `pos` (e.g. `1e999` parses to `Infinity`), in which case the bar position is silently reported as `null` instead of the message being rejected. Since `pos` is unconstrained in `os2lBeatSchema`, validate it as a finite/non-negative number in the schema rather than relying on this effectively-dead branch.

const slot = ((Math.floor(pos) % 4) + 4) % 4 + 1;
  return slot === 1 || slot === 2 || slot === 3 || slot === 4 ? slot : null;

packages/show-planner/src/compile.ts.content: The forced-impact branch fabricates a `substitute` verdict without ever calling `restrain()`. `restrain(..., { impact: true })` is what increments `wholeTrackImpactCount` / `sectionImpactCount` (restraint.ts lines 170-186), so on a failed white-hit draw the impact is emitted but not counted against the track/section impact budgets. Repeated drops therefore keep landing full-colour impacts past `trackImpactMax`, and the reported `budgetsUsed`/`budgetsRemaining` diverge from the cues actually emitted. Always call `restrain()` for budget accounting and then layer the draw decision on top of its verdict.

The event layer drops the `substitute` verdict for blackout/dip cues: only `reject` is handled, so a blackout that `restrain()` substitutes to `dip` (blackout too close to the previous one, restraint.ts lines 121-132) still falls through and is emitted as `blackout`. This defeats the blackout spacing constraint. Apply `r.verdict.substitute` as the emitted type (as the white-hit branch above does) instead of always re-emitting `p.cueType`.

packages/show-runtime/src/fastpath.ts.content: `aliasStore` defaults to a brand-new `MemoryAliasStore()` on every call. Since this store is what `resolveLiveTrack` learns alias mappings into, any caller that relies on the default silently starts from empty state each generation, so learned identity aliases never persist and resolution is repeated/degraded. Default to a module-level store (or make the parameter required) so identity state survives across generations.

Either set `installed: false` here or split the flag (e.g. `modelInstalled`) to make the partial state unambiguous.
